messages:
Marcus Lin: Dropping the threat model draft for offline bundle signing/verification. Main thing I want eyes on today: break-glass behavior + what we’re calling “fail-closed” in practice.

Marcus Lin: Link (restricted): confluence://security-and-compliance/secure-sdlc/threat-model-offline-artifact-signing

Marcus Lin: Questions for reviewers:
1) Should we allow any “skip verification” path at all?
2) If yes, what’s the strictest acceptable UX + audit story?
3) Do we need explicit downgrade prevention in v1 or can we defer?

Naomi Feldman: reading now. initial take: we can’t have “skip verification” as a casual flag. if we must have an override, it needs to be framed as policy exception + logged.

Connor O'Brien: +1 on not calling it “skip verification” in docs/CLI. Release Eng POV: we *will* hit corrupted media cases during pilots (zip/tar transfer issues, mirror bugs). Support will ask for a way forward, so break-glass may be necessary but it must hurt.

Ethan Park: installer UX note: we can implement as:
- always attempt verify
- if fail, print failure reason + how to rerun `verify`
- only then allow `--break-glass` to proceed
We should avoid “verify=false” config knobs.

Kevin Osei: from audit/control angle: break-glass is fine if it produces an immutable-ish record. need structured event that includes:
- bundle_id / release_version / manifest_digest
- failure_reason
- operator identity (best-effort)
- break_glass_used=true + reason text
Also: make sure it can’t be suppressed with `--quiet`.

Olga Petrov: +1. Also we need consistent language for customer acknowledgement (compliance posture / policy exception). I’ll want to reuse the exact same sentence in the exception policy page + installer prompt + docs.

Hanae Suzuki: key mgmt angle: override must NOT allow trusting a different key silently. e.g. “accept any signature” is a hard no.
Also: we should explicitly separate prod vs staging/test keys and fail if installer sees staging key unless a test-only config is set.

Marcus Lin: 👍 good call. in the threat model I currently have “separate staging/test key; never accepted by prod installer unless explicitly configured”. We should tighten that to: prod installer ships with prod trust roots only. any additional keys require explicit `--trust-key PATH` + fingerprint echo.

Naomi Feldman: can we also avoid environment-variable bypasses? (support will inevitably tell someone “set XYZ=1” and now we have untracked exceptions)

Ethan Park: yeah we can make it CLI-only. no env var. plus require interactive acknowledgement unless `--non-interactive` is set, in which case you must pass the acknowledgement string verbatim.

Connor O'Brien: re: “ack string verbatim” — please do. automation in air-gapped is very scripted; people will run non-interactive. but we can force `--break-glass --ack "I ACKNOWLEDGE..." --reason "..."`.

Kevin Osei: also require a reference ID in non-interactive mode (ticket number, change request). Even if it’s just a freeform `--ref` field.

SecurityBot: Reminder: Any break-glass functionality requires Security review before merge (CODEOWNERS: @marcus.lin @naomi.feldman). Please attach threat model + exception policy link in PR description.

Marcus Lin: ok, proposal for break-glass semantics:
- Default behavior: verification is mandatory; installer fails before unpack/install.
- If verification fails, operator may re-run with `--break-glass`.
- `--break-glass` requires:
  - `--ack <exact_string>` (non-empty and must match exact phrase)
  - `--reason <freeform>`
  - `--ref <ticket/change>` (required in non-interactive mode)
- Always emits an audit record locally + to cluster events when cluster is reachable.
- Warning text explicitly says: “This may violate your organization’s software integrity policy.”

Naomi Feldman: close. but I’d like the UX to force the operator to see the failure reason before overriding. i.e. we should still run verification first (don’t allow `--break-glass` to short-circuit execution path).

Ethan Park: yes. Implementation detail: even if `--break-glass` is set, we still attempt verify and we log the failure reason. Only then do we proceed.

Connor O'Brien: 👍 and make sure “verify only” is its own command too (`installer verify-bundle ...`) so customers can validate media ahead of maintenance.

Marcus Lin: already in draft requirements: “verify-only command to validate media before window” — will make it explicit.

Olga Petrov: can we add wording that break-glass is allowed only for “availability emergencies” and requires approval? Even if we can’t enforce approval in code, docs/policy must say it.

Naomi Feldman: yes. policy will say: requires customer security approver + Redwood support escalation for regulated accounts.

Kevin Osei: logging details: I want exact fields nailed down. Suggest we standardize event name now so docs + SIEM parsing doesn’t change.
Something like:
`event_type=offline_bundle_verification`
`result=success|failure|override`
If override, include `override_reason` and `override_ack_hash` (hash of ack string) so we can detect tampering? (or at least confirm exact prompt)

Ethan Park: we can do `override_acknowledged=true` and log the exact expected phrase ID/version rather than the text (avoid localization issues later).

Marcus Lin: good. we can version the ack phrase as `ack_policy_version=v1` and include the hash of the policy text shipped in the installer.

Hanae Suzuki: on key distribution: do we want the installer to ship with pinned public key fingerprint? otherwise customers can swap the key file and we “verify” attacker bundles.

Marcus Lin: yes. baseline: installer ships with embedded trust root(s) + prints fingerprint in `installer version` output. Optionally allow `--trust-key` but require fingerprint confirmation + treat as break-glass adjacent.

Naomi Feldman: +1. “--trust-key” should not be a normal path.

Connor O'Brien: careful: we do need a migration path for rotation (multiple trusted keys). But that’s different from “trust arbitrary key file.” If the installer ships a trust store with active+retired keys, that’s fine.

Hanae Suzuki: rotation plan: agree — ship multiple keys in trust store; deprecate old key in a later installer release. don’t make customers manage keys for v1.

Marcus Lin: ok, I’ll update threat model language:
- prod installer trust store includes active + retiring Redwood keys
- supports multiple key IDs
- no arbitrary key trust without explicit config, and treated as exception

Ethan Park: downgrades: right now our installer can be used to install older bundle if someone points it at one. do we want to block downgrades by default?

Naomi Feldman: yes. downgrade = replay risk. even offline we can do local state.

Connor O'Brien: I’m slightly worried about bricking recovery for customers who *need* rollback in air-gapped env. But we can have a “rollback” command that itself is break-glass + logs.

Kevin Osei: +1. From controls POV:
- default blocks downgrade
- rollback is explicit workflow
- rollback always emits audit event + requires `--ref`

Marcus Lin: makes sense. I’ll add to sign-off criteria: downgrade protection must exist in v1. Doesn’t need online freshness, but must prevent accidental rollbacks.

Ethan Park: implementation idea: store last installed version in cluster ConfigMap (control namespace). For first install (no state) allow. For upgrades compare semver.
If user wants rollback: `installer rollback --bundle ... --break-glass ...`.

Naomi Feldman: good. Also: canonicalization / “equivalent JSON” issues. Do we have a plan for deterministic signing payload?

Connor O'Brien: in release tooling we can enforce canonical JSON serialization + sorted keys. But we should also “deny unknown fields” on signed payload schema.

Marcus Lin: yes, I want that in threat model and as a PR gate. “Unknown fields rejected” prevents someone from smuggling in ambiguous semantics.

Olga Petrov: can we capture sign-off criteria in one place? I can link it from the exception policy + control mapping.

Marcus Lin: posting draft sign-off checklist here; tell me what’s missing:

Marcus Lin: Security sign-off criteria (v1) for offline bundle verification + break-glass:
1) Verification runs before any unpack/install; fail-closed default.
2) Signature verified against embedded Redwood trust store; supports multiple Redwood keys for rotation.
3) Manifest digest + per-artifact digests verified; no partial success.
4) Installer installs ONLY artifacts enumerated in manifest; unexpected executables rejected/ignored.
5) Break-glass does not bypass verification attempt; it only permits continuing after a logged failure.
6) Break-glass requires explicit acknowledgement (policy versioned), reason, and ref (ticket/change) in non-interactive.
7) Break-glass always emits structured audit event locally; cannot be silenced.
8) Downgrades blocked by default; rollback is separate explicit flow and requires break-glass.
9) Staging/test keys never accepted by prod installer.
10) No env-var bypasses for verification/override.

Kevin Osei: add: event fields are stable + documented. and include bundle_id, release_version, manifest_digest, key_id, result, failure_reason, break_glass_used, ack_policy_version, reason, ref.

Ethan Park: add: exit codes are stable too (support scripts rely on it). `verify` returns distinct exit codes for sig fail vs digest mismatch vs schema validation.

Connor O'Brien: add: CI integration test that generates bundle -> signs -> verifies in offline mode + a negative test where one file is modified.

Naomi Feldman: add: the acknowledgement text must explicitly say “you are installing unverified software artifacts” (not “verification failed” vaguely). And docs must warn that this may invalidate compliance.

Hanae Suzuki: add: signer key usage is KMS/HSM non-exportable + least privilege (even if not enforced by installer, it’s part of overall control story). But I assume that’s in the pipeline doc.

Marcus Lin: yep pipeline doc covers key custody; but I’ll mirror the key constraints in the threat model “assumptions/mitigations”.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: catching up. This looks directionally right. I’m ok with break-glass existing IF:
- it’s painful + explicit
- it’s auditable
- we can tell customers “default is fail-closed” without footnotes
Please make sure the customer-facing guide uses consistent language with Olga/Naomi.

Naomi Feldman: 👍 I’ll take an action to draft the required acknowledgement language and share with Ethan for the prompt.

Ethan Park: perfect. once we get that string, I’ll wire it into the CLI prompt + `--ack` exact match.

Connor O'Brien: I’ll update release engineering tasks to include canonical JSON and deny-unknown-fields checks in manifest/signing payload generation.

Kevin Osei: I’ll open a small issue to define the event schema + where it lands (local file path + optional k8s event). want to avoid putting it only in stdout.

Marcus Lin: thanks all. I’ll revise the threat model today with:
- explicit downgrade/rollback section
- “no env var bypass” requirement
- key distribution/trust store language
- logging fields + ack policy versioning

Marcus Lin: Naomi/Aisha — once revisions are in, can I get a 👍 in-thread for security sign-off to proceed with implementation PRs (installer + pipeline)?

Naomi Feldman: 👍 once the updated threat model reflects the checklist + I see the final ack language in it.

Dr. Aisha Rahman: 👍 same. If checklist is met and exception policy is linked, proceed.

SecurityBot: Action items detected:
- @marcus.lin update threat model with break-glass + downgrade requirements
- @naomi.feldman draft acknowledgement language
- @ethan.park implement CLI prompt + non-interactive flags
- @kevin.osei define audit event schema + retention location
- @connor.obrien ensure canonical serialization + deny-unknown-fields in signing payload
(Reply with “done” to clear)
